title: Homocysteine lowering with folic acid and B vitamins in vascular disease
authors: Lonn E, Yusuf S, Arnold MJ, Sheridan P, Pogue J, Micks M, et al.
population: Patients aged 55 years or older with vascular disease or diabetes in Canada and the USA (with fortification) and Brazil, western Europe and Slovakia (without); supplements above 0.2 mg folic acid excluded
funder: Supported by a Canadian Institutes of Health Research Grant (MT-15418) and in-kind contributions by Jamieson Laboratories, Canada. The study sponsors were not involved in the design, execution, analysis, or reporting of the trial results.
inKindSupport: Study drug and matching placebo were provided by Jamieson Laboratories, Canada.
authorConflicts: No potential conflict of interest relevant to this article was reported.
result: Folic acid 2.5 mg, vitamin B6 50 mg and B12 1 mg daily against placebo. Homocysteine fell by 2.4 µmol/L against a rise of 0.8. Cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke in 519 (18.8%) against 547 (19.8%): RR 0.95 (95% CI 0.84 to 1.07). Stroke RR 0.75 (0.59 to 0.97). Hospitalisation for unstable angina RR 1.24 (1.04 to 1.49).
